'''Herbert Glejser''' (2 January 1938 – 20 January 2024) was a Belgian economist and [[Econometrics|econometrician]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2024 |title=Herbert Glejser - Obituary |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S001429212400196X |journal=European Economic Review |doi=10.1016/j.euroecorev.2024.104867 |issn=0014-2921|url-access=subscription |doi-access=free }}</ref> Early in his career, he became known for the [[Glejser test]], a statistics test for [[Homoscedasticity and heteroscedasticity|heteroskedasticity]] he developed in 1969.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Oxford Dictionary of Economics |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=2017 |isbn=9780198759430 |edition=5th}}</ref> He was an Economics professor in Belgium until 2003 and had been visiting professor in several US universities ([[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley University]], [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]]), as well as in Brazil, Germany and Israel. He was the founder and first editor of the ''[[European Economic Review]]'', one of the oldest economics journals in Europe, with Jean Waelbroeck.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Erreygers |first=G. |title=The New Palgrave Dictionary of Economics |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan |year=2018 |isbn=978-1-349-95188-8 |location=London |pages=3416–3420 |chapter=Economics in Belgium}}</ref>

== Biography ==

=== Early life ===
Herbert Glejser was born on {{date|January 2, 1938}} in [[Vienna (Austria)|Vienna]], [[Austria]], from a [[Jews|Jewish]] family. The [[Anschluss]] on {{date|March 12, 1938}} forced his parents to flee from Austria and seek refuge in [[Belgium]].<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last1=Lobet |first1=Marcel |date=March 26, 1955 |title=Un adolescent entr'ouvre ses 'cahiers de poésie': La rencontre à l'aube par Herbert Glejser |work=Le Soir}}</ref> The Glejser family obtained Belgian citizenship in 1955.

After his high school studies in [[:fr: Athénée royal de Bruxelles|Athénée royal de Bruxelles]], Herbert Glejser started University at the age of 16, at the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]] (ULB) in the Social, Political and Economical Sciences Departement. Simultaneously, he enrolled in a degree in Business Engineering at the École de Commerce Solvay (now [[Solvay Brussels School of Economics and Management]]). In 1958, aged 20, he received his BA in Commercial Engineering and in March 1963, then 25, completed his PhD in Economics.

=== Academic life ===
In 1959, aged 21, Herbert Glejser was hired as Secretary and [[Research fellow]] at the Department in Applied Economics of ULB (DULBEA), the research centre of the Solvay Brussels School of Economics and Management and the Université libre de Bruxelles.

Assistant Professor at the ULB from 1963, Herbert Glejser became a full Professor in Economics in 1969, aged 31.

His interest focused in [[Applied Statistics|applied statistics]] and [[macroeconomics]] and, in 1981, he became one of the few Belgian economists to support the devaluation of the [[Belgian franc]], despite the views of the [[Banque nationale de Belgique|National Bank of Belgium]].''<ref>Paul Hatry, sénateur, Annales du Sénat de Belgique, Séance du 2 mars 1982, {{p.|567}}  https://www.senate.be/handann/S0016/S00163862/S00163862.pdf</ref>'' Glejser deemed this measure inevitable to save "''this impossible monster the Belgian economy had become".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Glejser |first1=Herbert |last2=Waelbroeck |first2=Jean |date=1982 |title=Du nouveau franc au renouveau économique: ébauche d'un programme |url=https://dipot.ulb.ac.be/dspace/bitstream/2013/12487/1/ber-0611.pdf |journal=Brussels Economic Review |issue=94 |pages=163–185 |access-date= |via=IDEAS}}</ref>'' The Belgian franc has later been devalued, in February 1982''.''

In Belgium, from 1969, Herbert Glejser taught in Brussels universities (ULB and [[Vrije Universiteit Brussel|VUB]]) and from 1974 at the [[Université de Namur|Facultés universitaires Notre-Dame de la Paix]], in [[Namur]]. Abroad, he has been [[Distinguished visiting professor|visiting Professor]] in the United States, notably at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in 1970 and 1974, at [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1970, at [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) in 1991; in Israel at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in 1980-1981; in Germany at [[LMU Munich]] and in Brazil at the [[Federal University of Minas Gerais]], in 1996.

Council Member and Emeritus fellow of the [[European Economic Association]] from 1986 to 1990,<ref>{{cite web |title=Emeritus fellows |url=https://www.eeassoc.org/fellows |website=European Economic Association}}</ref> Glejser has been a Consultant for the [[European Economic Community]] from 1993.{{citation needed|date=November 2023}}

=== Honors and awards ===
Herbert Glejser received the [[Fulbright Program]] scholarship in 1974, a visiting scholar grant in [[Harvard University]] for his project research on "Econometric analysis of American capital abroad".<ref>{{cite web | url=https://fulbrightscholars.org/grantee/herbert-glejser | title=Herbert Glejser &#124; Fulbright Scholar Program }}</ref> He was awarded a Professor Chair from the [[Francqui Foundation]] in 1982-1983, and won the Pommerehne Prize from the [[Association for Cultural Economics International]] (ACEI) in 2002 for his article ''Efficiency and inefficiency in the ranking in competitions: The case of the Queen Elisabeth Music Contest'', co-written with economist Bruno Heyndels.<ref>{{cite news |title=Herbert Glejser: 'Elisabethwedstrijd verloopt niet eerlijk' |url=https://www.demorgen.be/nieuws/herbert-glejser-elisabethwedstrijd-verloopt-niet-eerlijk~bc5a4299/ |work=De Morgen |date=5 October 2002}}</ref>

=== Glejser test ===
Herbert Glejser published ''A New Test for Heteroskedasticity'' in March 1969 in the ''[[Journal of the American Statistical Association]]''<ref name=":02">Glejser, Herbert (1969), A New Test for Heteroskedasticity, Journal of the American Statistical Association, 64:325, 316-323, DOI: 10.1080/01621459.1969.10500976</ref> where he develops a new test for [[Homoscedasticity and heteroscedasticity|heteroskedasticity]], derived from the [[Park test]] that had been published by Rolla Edward Park in [[Econometrica]] in 1966<ref>Park, R. E. (1966). "Estimation with Heteroscedastic Error Terms". ''Econometrica''. '''34''' (4): 888. JSTOR 1910108</ref>

Glejser measures his test against the [[Goldfeld–Quandt test]] (1965): ''"[T]he new test seems to compare favourably, except perhaps in the case of large samples."''<ref name=":02" />

In 1996, [[Leslie G. Godfrey|Leslie George Godfrey]] has shown that the Glejser test for heteroskedasticity was valid only under conditional symmetry, and suggested some modifications.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Godfrey |first1=Leslie G. |title=Some results on the Glejser and Koenker tests for heteroskedasticit |journal=Journal of Econometrics |date=1996 |volume=72 |issue=1–2 |pages=275–299|doi=10.1016/0304-4076(94)01723-9 }}</ref> Improvements to the Glejser test have later been developed by Kyung So Im<ref>Im, Kyung So, (2000), Robustifying Glejser test of heteroskedasticity, Journal of Econometrics, 97, issue 1, 179-188</ref> and by José António Machado and João Santos Silva<ref>Machado, José António and Santos Silva, João, (2000), Glejser's test revisited, Journal of Econometrics, 97, issue 1, 189-202</ref>

In 2020, the Glejser test was used to test the [[Dunning–Kruger effect|Dunning-Kruger]] hypothesis.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gignac |first1=Gilles E. |last2=Zajenkowski |first2=Marcin |title=The Dunning-Kruger effect is (mostly) a statistical artefact: Valid approaches to testing the hypothesis with individual differences data |journal=Intelligence |date=2020 |volume=80 |doi=10.1016/j.intell.2020.101449 |s2cid=216410901 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0160289620300271|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== European Economic Review ===

In 1969, Herbert Glejser and Jean Waelbroeck founded and became first editors of the ''[[European Economic Review]]'' (''EER'').<ref>{{cite journal |title=Une nouvelle revue économique européenne |journal=Économie et statistique |date=September 1969 |volume=4 |pages=71–72 |doi=10.3406/estat.1969.1826 |url=https://www.persee.fr/doc/estat_0336-1454_1969_num_4_1_1826}}</ref>

They remained sole editors from 1969 to 1986, while EER publishers changed from the International Association of Applied Economics (ASEPELT) to [[North Holland|North-Holland]], then [[Elsevier]]. Over this period of time, over 10'000 article pages were selected by ca. 2'000 peer reviewers. In 1986, Glejser and Waelbroeck were joined by Peter Neary and Agnar Sandmo as associated editors.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Glejser |first1=Herbert |last2=Waelbroeck |first2=Jean |title=A few words to the readers |journal=European Economic Review |date=1986 |volume=30 |issue=1 |pages=1–3|doi=10.1016/0014-2921(86)90028-0 }}</ref> Jean Waelbroeck remained co-Editor-in-chief until 1991, Herbert Glejser for 25 years, until 1993.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Eckstein |first1=Zvi |last2=Gal-Or |first2=Esther |last3=Gylfason |first3=Thorvaldur |last4=Pfann |first4=Gerard A. |last5=von Hagen |first5=Juergen |title=A tribute to the founders |journal=European Economic Review |date=2006 |volume=50 |issue=1|pages=v |doi=10.1016/j.euroecorev.2005.11.001 }}</ref>
